clue.text: Suffering as Samson was, fatally

definitions.meaning: in pain or anguish, upset and troubled
Samson was deprived of his hair, which cost him his strength and in the end his life

explanation.surface: Someone is in agony, compared to the biblical strongman's fatal plight.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word: DIS (deprived of) + TRESSED (having locks). Delilah had Samson's hair cut off, leading to his capture and death.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in anguish or pain is a plain synonym of the adjective.

clue.text: Stupid daughter getting behind

parts.note: aft means at the back, behind

explanation.surface: A foolish girl is falling behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Silly or foolish is a direct synonym of this informal British adjective.

clue.text: Major port in south-east America

indicators.note: the port is placed inside the other letters

parts.note: SE is the compass abbreviation for south-east
US is the United States, America
Rio de Janeiro is a major port, often just Rio

explanation.surface: An important harbour located in the south-eastern US.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Major' looks like an adjective in the surface, but it is the definition, meaning grave.
explanation.definitionFit: Major as in significant or grave, as a serious problem is a major one.

clue.text: I ran sole army mobile military unit

indicators.note: mobile means moving, so the letters of the phrase move into a new order

explanation.surface: A commander says he ran a lone mobile army force.
explanation.walkthrough: The ROYAL MARINES are the British navy's amphibious infantry force.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Marines are the amphibious infantry corps of the British Navy, a fighting force.

clue.text: Bites uppish friend in the back

indicators.note: in a down clue, upward means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: nips are small bites
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: An arrogant friend bites someone in the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uppish' looks like snooty; in a down clue it turns NIPS upwards to SPIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the backbone, the spine is the back, so an adverb meaning in that region.

clue.text: Cleansing procedures adopted by hygiene master

indicators.note: the letters are held within the run of these two words

explanation.surface: A cleanliness expert has taken up cleaning routines.
explanation.definitionFit: Injections of fluid to flush the bowel are medical cleansing treatments.

clue.text: A person on foot took off

parts.note: PED is short for pedestrian, someone walking

explanation.surface: Someone walking set off, or perhaps an aircraft took off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Took off' looks like departing; here it means mimicked.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone off is to imitate or mimic them, a meaning shared by the verb.

clue.text: Word in email regularly seen in plain language

indicators.note: the picked letters appear inside the other word

parts.note: prose is ordinary, plain written language as opposed to verse

indicators.note: every other letter of email is taken, the second and fourth

explanation.surface: A word in an email that shows up often in straightforward writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes M and I from email.
explanation.definitionFit: To give one's word is to make a pledge or vow.

clue.text: It gets confused with talented amateur

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters of it and talented are jumbled together

explanation.surface: Something is mistaken for a gifted non-professional.
explanation.definitionFit: A dabbler who pursues an art without professional commitment is an amateur.

clue.text: Try on manoeuvres adopted by superior gold-digger

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are taken into the middle of the other word

parts.note: finer means better, of superior quality

indicators.note: the words try on are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to get on in society through clever moves to land a rich partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gold-digger' suggests a fortune-hunting partner, but here it means a literal prospector.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospector in the 1849 California gold rush was called by this name, a literal miner seeking gold.

clue.text: Shared resources Hank's taken back

indicators.note: the word for hank is read backwards

parts.note: a hank is a coil or loop of yarn or rope

explanation.surface: A man called Hank has had communal funds returned to him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hank' looks like a man's name; it is a coil of yarn.
explanation.definitionFit: A common fund or stock that several people contribute to and draw on is a collective kitty.

clue.text: Mozart work aunt is playing with octet around France

indicators.note: the anagram goes around the single letter
the letters play about into a new arrangement

parts.note: F is the international vehicle code for France

explanation.surface: An aunt performs Mozart with an eight-piece ensemble surrounding a French player.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of AUNT IS OCTET wraps round F.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosi Fan Tutte is a comic opera by Mozart, first performed in 1790.

clue.text: Perhaps hen is female bird

parts.note: an owl is a bird

explanation.surface: A hen, being female, counts as a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen is an example of domestic poultry, hence 'Perhaps' signals an instance.

clue.text: A military alliance film person dealing with bodies

parts.note: NATO is the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, a military alliance
a film is a thin layer or haze, like mist

explanation.surface: A defence pact, a movie and someone who handles corpses make a strange list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' suggests a movie; here it is a thin coating or haze.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist who studies the structure of the body, often by dissection, fits this description.

clue.text: Cowboy comfortable coming up with delay

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word is read upwards, so reversed

parts.note: snug means cosy, comfortable
to linger is to delay or dawdle

explanation.surface: A rancher settles in comfortably and dawdles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming up' turns SNUG upwards to GUNS.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunfighter of the Wild West is one kind of cowboy figure.

clue.text: Dicky heading off from Bedfordshire town

indicators.note: the first letter, the head, of the town is removed

parts.note: Dunstable is a town in Bedfordshire, an English county north of London

explanation.surface: Someone called Dicky is setting out from a town in Bedfordshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a name; it is British slang for shaky or unreliable. DUNSTABLE is a town in Bedfordshire, a county north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Dicky is informal British for weak or unsound, as in a dicky heart, so wobbly.

clue.text: Spies taking rebellious soldiers in films

indicators.note: the agency's letters take the others inside them

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency, a body of spies

indicators.note: rebels turn against authority, so the word for soldiers is turned round

parts.note: men are soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: Intelligence agents recruit mutinous troops, as happens in movies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Men' for soldiers is the ranks as against officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Films collectively, or the movie industry and art form, are known by this name.

clue.text: Conflict is right in novels

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the word for novels

parts.note: novels are fiction

explanation.surface: Disputes over whether a book's stance is correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Friction is disagreement or clashing between people, so conflict.

clue.text: Type that is breaking out?

definitions.note: a noun phrase here: a breaking out, an attack from a besieged position

parts.note: a sort is a type or kind
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A query about what kind of thing counts as escaping.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is a slightly loose description.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally by troops from a besieged place is a breaking out to attack.

clue.text: Roll filled with old poultry?

definitions.note: a single bird stands for poultry, an example, hence the question mark

indicators.note: the list contains the single letter

parts.note: a roster is a roll or list of names

explanation.surface: A bread roll is stuffed with leftover chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roll' looks like bread; it is a list.
explanation.definitionFit: A male domestic chicken is one bird among the poultry, an example signalled by the query.

clue.text: One often works on Sunday, roasting nuts

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters of roasting go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone works weekends, cooking nuts over a fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roasting nuts' reads as cooking; 'nuts' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A church musician typically plays at Sunday services, so works then.

clue.text: Set up where horse might be at start of race

definitions.meaning: to set up is to fit or put in place

definitions.text: where horse might be at start of race
definitions.meaning: horses begin a race from starting stalls

explanation.surface: A description of a racehorse's position before the off.
explanation.definitionFit: To put equipment in place ready for use is to set it up.

clue.text: Opening note penned by German composer

indicators.note: penned means enclosed, as in a pen, so the note sits inside the composer

parts.note: Johann Sebastian Bach was a German composer
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A German composer wrote the first note of a work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penned' looks like written; it means enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: A gap or break in a wall or defence is an opening.

clue.text: Eroticism may provide such exercise

definitions.note: describes the type of exercise, so it stands for an adjective

indicators.note: the word can supply a different word once its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheeky suggestion that erotic activity counts as a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram indicator is unusually mild: 'may provide' says the letters of EROTICISM can be made into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Exercise where muscles push against a fixed resistance without moving is called by this adjective.

clue.text: What rough sea does to ship

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, placed before a ship's name

explanation.surface: A description of stormy waves buffeting a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as one description, but 'to ship' is wordplay; SS is the steamship prefix.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy waves fling and pitch things about, the verb meaning throw around.

clue.text: Doctor embracing the old? One adds colour

indicators.note: the doctor's letters hug the other word

parts.note: ye is an old form of the

explanation.surface: A physician hugs an elderly patient, who brightens things up.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tints fabric or hair for a living gives it colour.

clue.text: Follower of post-punk style obtained heroin initially

parts.note: got means obtained

indicators.note: only the first letter of heroin is taken

explanation.surface: A fan of dark post-punk music got hold of drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan of the gloomy post-punk music and black-clad fashion of the 1980s is so called.

clue.text: Mark a point with sharp beaks

definitions.note: plural noun; magistrates as a collective body

parts.note: M is an abbreviation for mark, as in the German currency
the gist is the main point
racy can mean lively, sharp or piquant

explanation.surface: Someone notes a point using pointed bird bills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beaks' looks like birds' bills; it is old British slang for magistrates or judges.
explanation.definitionFit: Collectively the justices of the peace form this body, and beak is slang for a justice.

clue.text: Unusual alternative forms of sun god

parts.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god
the plural forms signals both spellings, so the alternative spelling Re follows the usual one

explanation.surface: Uncommon variant names exist for the deity of the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: The Egyptian sun god has two spellings, and the clue asks for both; 'alternative forms of' supplies the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seldom found or met is uncommon, the simple synonym.

clue.text: Person handling money could make fortune returning wad of notes

parts.note: chance means fortune or luck

indicators.note: the word for the wad comes back, read in reverse

parts.note: a roll is a wad of banknotes

explanation.surface: A cashier could make a fortune by handing back a stack of banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' turns ROLL into LLOR.
explanation.definitionFit: The British finance minister is the Chancellor of the Exchequer, who controls the nation's money.
